What happens to my Dropbox when I die?

Short answer: Dropbox may give access to a deceased person's files, but only after reviewing proof of death and a valid court order showing you have a legal right to them. Access isn't guaranteed and can take time. Dropbox's own first suggestion is to check the person's computer, where the Dropbox folder often holds a synced copy of every file.

Key facts

  • Check the synced folder on their computer first
  • Needs proof of death + court order
  • Access not guaranteed
  • Request via a Dropbox support ticket

How do I prepare my Dropbox account?

  1. Check the deceased person's computer for a synced Dropbox folder first.
  2. Contact Dropbox support with your ID, proof of death, relationship and a valid court order.
  3. For yourself: share key folders with family now and store your password in a vault with emergency access.

Read the official policy ↗

What documents do heirs need?

  • Full name and Dropbox email of the deceased
  • Your name, mailing address, email and relationship
  • A photocopy of your government ID
  • A valid court order establishing your right to the files

How long does it take?

Dropbox says these requests 'can take some time' and gives no fixed timeframe.

What can't be recovered?

  • Files that only exist online, if the request is refused
